passage:
A city held a river festival after years of cleaning its polluted river. People could walk along new paths, watch boat shows, and join science activities.
Older residents remembered when the river smelled bad and no one wanted to stand near it. Children saw only the cleaner version.
The festival included photos from the polluted years so people would not forget.
The river's recovery was not quick. It required rules, money, cleaning, and changes by factories and homes.
The festival celebrated success, but also responsibility. A clean river is not a gift that stays clean by itself. It is a relationship that must be maintained.
